reasons: The cited clause (p0026, first §7.2) imposes a disclose-and-match obligation before Customer may engage another provider, which operates as a right of first refusal / de facto restraint on our freedom to source; it is unlimited as to product category and duration and has no performance-based exit, so it fails the EXCLUSIVITY fallback and is correctly classified as a deviation rather than an acceptable fallback.

Redline is the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position — full deletion of the offending sentence — and leaves the unrelated payment-terms §7.2 (p0027) untouched; deterministic checks confirm no residual sole-supplier/requirements obligation on Customer.
Comment is accurate, correctly scoped and appropriately toned: it states what was removed, why it is an exclusivity restraint, and anchors on §12.3's express no-exclusivity acknowledgement.

Double-flagging is adequately addressed: the rationale explains the clause is raised as a sourcing restraint rather than an MFN pricing term, and confirms the other 'exclusive' references (licence scope, remedies, jurisdiction) are not exclusive dealing.

Note only: §12.3 already disclaims any exclusivity commitment, so the practical risk is contradiction/ambiguity rather than a clean exclusive-dealing covenant — deletion remains the right fix, but the effective severity is somewhat mitigated.
